note: Field names, stat keys and union values follow src/domain. Percentages are decimals. Descriptions stay verbatim. Every mechanic is also carried as values: a grant names its recipient and its stats, params carry the numbers a condition needs, and combat says whether the entry changes anything inside a fight.

sources.lolchess.gg: units and their abilities; the Set 18 wisp and augment pools, with gold, tier, category and appearance condition
sources.metatft.com: trait descriptions, augment stages and the augment category taxonomy
sources.communitydragon.org: Riot data, PBE snapshot dated 2026-07-31. Trait names and breakpoints, wisp identifiers and variables, timeless item stats, and the 29 augments this set brought of its own
sources.tactics.tools: an earlier build — it still says Eldritch, Sunbeam and Moonbeam. Read to date the other sources, never to value them

set-18/units.json.verified: 65 units, 14/13/14/14/10 by cost, plus six summoned entities. Traits agree with traits.json in both directions. Kobuko and Alune match Community Dragon on every stat. Every ability carries the numbers its tooltip states outside the breakdown. Four stars are a 1-, 2- and 3-cost affair: all 41 of them carry a fourth value, none of the 4- and 5-costs does

set-18/traits.json.verified: 36 names against Community Dragon, no divergence either way, and 34 of the 36 breakpoint ladders identical. Rosters cover the 65 units. Every breakpoint carries its grants and its parameters, read from the tooltip

set-18/wisps.json.verified: The client defines 181 charms; the published sources carried 163 of them, and gold, category and description agree on those. 84 change a fight and are decomposed into grants. The 14 the aggregators omit are economy — gold, experience, player health, streaks — and were added from the client on 2026-08-14 with their name, their cost and their values. Their category, description and appearance window stay null: those live on an object the extraction cannot name yet. Crystal Ball is ours alone and has no counterpart in the client

timeless/augments.json.verified: 255 distinct augments across 257 rows: Beast Within and Beast Within+ each appear twice, same tier and same apparition, differing only in the champion they hand out — Sivir or Nidalee. lolchess and metatft agree on every name and every tier. 240 matched to Riot Set 18 entries; 99 carry combat effects and are decomposed into grants

timeless/items.json.verified: 137 items: 10 components, 39 craftables, 20 emblems, 32 artifacts, 36 radiants. The eight-by-eight grid is closed. Seven stat lines corrected against Community Dragon

more.adaptor: Their main stats (AP or AD) can vary, therefor, scaling key accept only an array as value.
more.keyword: Default base keywords such as Wounds, Burn, Sunder, Shred, Chill, Slow etc... Does not hold a value directlyt into the JSON because It would violate DRY principle. So it's a name to retrieve when used
more.id: Kebab-case slug, the casing the rest of the vocabulary uses, because the engine reads an id as a Record key and nothing else. Set content is prefixed by its set — s18-adaptor, s18-akali — so a Set 19 trait of the same name lands beside it rather than on top of it; timeless content is not. Apostrophes and punctuation drop, a trailing + becomes -plus, roman numerals stay: rek-sai, thiefs-gloves, celestial-blessing-i, champ-delivery-plus. Two augments share a name and differ by the champion they hand out, so their slug carries it: beast-within-sivir, beast-within-nidalee.
more.iconPath: One versioned file per entry, taken from the client. wisps.json carries none — a wisp is text. Lux is one entry with ten variants and ten icons, so the path sits on the variant wherever variants exist.
more.combat: True when the engine can read the entry and produce an exact number from it. The Coven trait is false: holding it grants no combat bonus, only essence. The Coven Acolyte augment is true. Composition effects are false — Apex Predator takes team slots, Avatar counts double towards breakpoints, neither lands inside a fight.
more.requiresRunInput: True when the entry carries a state no calculation derives and no player can reproduce on demand: a choice taken during a run, or a counter carried across rounds. The user declares it before the fight, and the data enumerates the options without designating one. What each entry expects is written beside it here.
more.team: A grant to team excludes the trait holders. Juggernaut at six gives its Juggernauts 34% durability and everyone else 8% — never the sum.
more.prose: The catalog files carry data and nothing else. A remark, a caveat, an observation — anything a reader needs and a parser does not — lives here instead, keyed by what it explains. Nine note fields were lifted out of traits.json and units.json on 2026-08-11; what follows is what they said.
more.summonScaling: A summoned entity scales off the trait that brought it, through the formula its scaling field states. Two rules the formula does not show: a duplicated champion counts once towards the trait's star total, and flat team bonuses land after the scaling rather than before. Elderwood plants take a third factor the trait never mentions — the stage multiplies their health on a curve of its own, one per plant, so the same board reads differently at stage two and at stage six.
more.null: A field set to null is a question the extraction asked and could not answer, told apart from a field that is absent because the entry has no use for it. Fourteen wisps carry three of them — category, description and appears — because the client keeps those on an object whose property names a shipped build strips out.
more.upgraded: A wisp has three states: taken, upgraded, and prismatic. Blossom upgrades every wisp from three onwards, so the upgraded value is not an edge case. Where the client gives both, the second lands beside the first under the same name with an Upgraded suffix.
more.byStar: A plant's series is indexed by its own star level, not by the tier of the trait that summoned it. Elderwood sets that star level itself: one up to seven, two at nine, three at eleven. Series that stop before three do so because the client's curve repeats its last value, not because a value is missing.
more.covenEssence: The Coven trait is economy on its own. Dark Ritual and Coven Acolyte are what turn its essence into combat power.
more.blackthorn: traitBonusMultiplier amplifies the sacrifice table alone; the team health grant is flat per breakpoint. It grows with the breakpoint rather than repeating — 1 at two, 1.25 at four, 1.5 at six.
more.description: Written for a tooltip, not for a paragraph. Sections are separated by a blank line — passive, active, per-breakpoint scale, and any keyword it leans on. Inside a section, a line break every proposition, so no line runs long enough to wrap. Numbers are references into breakdown rather than literals: the engine recomputes them against the stats of the moment, and a figure frozen at one star with no items is wrong as soon as anything modifies it.
